title: A Monsoon for the Provision
premise: Ulyana Iversen, a railroad engineer who has spent fifteen years surveying closed lines to avoid the world, discovers a tide-revealed cave on the coast of a concession territory whose permits expire in one monsoon season. Inside is evidence that the river feeding the region's rail line rises from a source the concession company has forbidden and falsified records about. When his young stowaway apprentice, Tam, is endangered by the company's enforcers, Ulyana must choose between loyalty to the crew that became his found family and exposing the truth that will destroy their livelihoods. He follows the river upstream through the monsoon, publishes the true maps at the source, and returns to find the crew—though scattered by the scandal—chooses him over the company, ending with the family reunited as the first honest train crosses the corrected line.
about_author: Kestrel Halloran is a former hydrographic surveyor who spent a decade mapping rivers in monsoon country before turning to fiction. Halloran writes adventure novels where landscapes keep secrets and the people who measure them must decide what the measurements are worth.

chapters.title: The Tide Keeps No Records
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. While surveying a closed coastal spur before the concession expires, he witnesses an extreme low tide expose a sea cave bearing carved markers older than any company chart. Taking rubbings, he hides them from his foreman, but his apprentice Tam sees everything. Emotional beat: wonder cracking open fifteen years of deliberate invisibility; Ulyana feels the map in his hands become a question instead of an answer.

chapters.title: Miles Are Not Years
chapters.summary: Alternating Ulyana and Tam POVs. The cave rubbings match discrepancies in the concession's sealed river surveys—the source is forbidden because it proves the company built the line on falsified water rights. Enforcers board the work camp searching for 'stolen documents.' Ulyana lies to protect Tam; Tam, hurt by the lie, nearly turns himself in. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth begin pulling apart, and Ulyana realizes silence now endangers the family he never meant to make.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Monsoon
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with interludes from the foreman Brannoc. Ulyana flees upriver with Tam to reach the source before the permits lapse and the cave floods forever. Brannoc, ordered to stop them, wrestles between duty and love for his crew. A rope bridge fails in the storm; Tam nearly drowns saving the maps. Emotional beat: climax—Ulyana reaches the source, verifies the truth at cost of almost losing Tam, and chooses to publish rather than bury it.

chapters.title: A Monsoon for the Provision
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converging. The published maps void the concession; crews are dismissed and scattered, and Ulyana expects exile as the price of truth. But Brannoc arrives at the flooded cave mouth having refused a promotion to hunt him down, and the crew follows. As the rains end, they sign on to resurvey the line honestly under new ownership. Emotional beat: resolution—truth costs everything except each other; Ulyana finally measures life in years, not miles.
